To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the linear binding potential with the one-gluon correction is able to reproduce the experimental data for the meson masses, leptonic widths and mixing effects with a very good accuracy, for mesons of mass ≳1 Ge V.

the linear confinement potential, with the inclusion of the one-gluon-exchange interaction, is able to reproduce the meson mass spectrum for mesons of mass greater than 1 GeV, with the exception of the lightest mesons (π and K) for which the relativistic effects are not negligible.

the meson mass spectrum and leptonic widths of light and heavy meson systems, including the mixing effects, can be described in the framework of a relativistic linear potential model with one-gluonic exchange corrections.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the description of the light and heavy quark-antiquark meson spectrum, and the leptonic widths for the light mesons, by using a relativistic linear potential model with one-gluonic exchange corrections, in a gauge invariant theory.
the study of the properties of the mesonic sector of a gauge theory with a linear binding potential.
the study of the hadron spectrum in the framework of a gauge theory with a linear potential and one-gluon corrections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model under consideration provides a good qualitative understanding of the meson properties, and that the agreement with the data is satisfactory.

the linear potential, with the inclusion of relativistic corrections, is a good candidate to describe the spectrum of mesons, with a few limitations for the lighter particles, which can be improved by the inclusion of higher order terms in the expansion.

the linear confinement model, with one-gluons exchange corrections, is able to reproduce the meson masses with a precision of ≲ 10%, and the leptonic widths with a precision of 20% for the light mesons and ≲ 10% for the heavy mesons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the linear binding potential, together with one-gluons exchange corrections, is a suitable approach for the description of mesons with masses ≳1GeV, in a gauge theory framework.
, in a gauge theory with linear potential, the meson masses can be reproduced in a satisfactory way, but the leptonic widths are less well described.

, in the present approach, the linear potential is the main contribution for the description of the light meson masses, while the one-gluon-exchange corrections are more relevant to the description of heavy mesons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple linear binding potential with the one-gluon-exchange corrections, in combination with the relativistic corrections, is able to describe a wide variety of the meson properties.
the linear binding potential is a viable alternative to the Coulomb-plus-linear potential in the description of hadronic states.
a linear binding potential with a single parameter can describe the masses and widths of mesons of different flavours, with a good agreement to the experimental data.
